items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: But my favorite writers might be Ellington, Strayhorn, Gil Evans and George Russell.

ctx.x: Certain things. But I think everybody should know some kind of basic rules and then set out to break them. Because I’ve had like a seminar in my house with some really good professional writers and the point is they learned the rules but they never learned how to break them. So my purpose at that point would say well how do we break these rules? How do we do this and what can you tell us to get away from these things? Because you can write something very correct and it’ll sound boring as hell. And then you could…
basically what you do in a way. And then you hopefully steal enough and maybe fuse this into something of your own hopefully.
